en: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us. Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Amr ibn Abi Sufyan ibn Asid ibn Jariya al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhra and one of Abu Hurayra's companions, informed me that Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) sent a ten-man reconnaissance unit and appointed over them Asim ibn Thabit al-Ansari, the grandfather of Asim ibn Umar. They set out, and when they were at al-Had'a, between Usfan and Mecca, news of them reached a clan of Hudhayl called Banu Lihyan. They sent nearly two hundred men against them, all archers. They followed their tracks until they found their provisions, dates they had taken from Medina, and said: These are the dates of Yathrib. They followed their tracks, and when Asim and his companions saw them, they took refuge on a hill. The people surrounded them and said: Come down and surrender yourselves; you have our pledge and covenant that we will not kill any of you. Asim ibn Thabit, the commander of the unit, said: As for me, by Allah, I will not come down today under the protection of a disbeliever. O Allah, convey our news to Your Prophet. They shot arrows at them and killed Asim and seven others. Three men came down to them under the pledge and covenant, among them Khubayb al-Ansari, Ibn Dathina, and another man. When they had them under control, they loosened the strings of their bows and bound them. The third man said: This is the beginning of treachery. By Allah, I will not accompany you; in these dead men there is an example for me. They dragged him and tried to make him accompany them, but he refused, so they killed him. They went on with Khubayb and Ibn Dathina until they sold them in Mecca after the battle of Badr. The descendants of al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf bought Khubayb, for Khubayb had killed al-Harith ibn Amir on the day of Badr. Khubayb remained their captive. Ubaydullah ibn Iyad informed me that the daughter of al-Harith informed him: When they gathered, Khubayb borrowed a razor from me to shave with, and I lent it to him. He took one of my sons while I was unaware. When I came to him, I found him sitting on his thigh with the razor in his hand. I was terrified, and Khubayb recognized the fear on my face. He said: Are you afraid that I will kill him? I would never do that. By Allah, I have never seen a captive better than Khubayb. By Allah, I once found him eating from a bunch of grapes in his hand while he was shackled in iron, although there was no fruit in Mecca. She used to say: It was provision from Allah that He gave Khubayb. When they took him out of the sacred territory to kill him in the open land, Khubayb said to them: Let me pray two units. They let him, and he prayed two units. Then he said: Were it not that you might think what I am experiencing is fear, I would have lengthened them. O Allah, count them one by one. I do not care when I am killed as a Muslim, on which side I fall for Allah. That is for the sake of the Deity, and if He wills, He may bless the torn limbs of a mutilated body. The son of al-Harith killed him. Khubayb thus established the practice of two prayer units for every Muslim killed in captivity. Allah answered the prayer of Asim ibn Thabit on the day he was killed. The Prophet (peace be upon him) informed his Companions of their story and what had happened to them. Some of the disbelieving Quraysh, having been told that Asim had been killed, sent people to bring back a part of him by which he could be identified, for he had killed one of their prominent men on the day of Badr. A swarm like a canopy of hornets was sent against Asim, and it protected him from their messengers, so they could not cut anything from his flesh.
